A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Bullet Trains study. Their main text, Appendices A–G, equations, 13 figures, and five tables are readable and matchable despite pagination changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original trained-model accuracies, GPU timing experiments, Yin-Yang temporal-discretization experiments, and spike-consumption/work analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and reports revised SHD/SSC accuracies and spike-consumption diagnostics.

M1.justification: Appendix E.1 adds an individual neuron-and-instance over-firing penalty to the training objective, supplementing the existing batch-average regularizer. v1 described targeting outlier neurons as future work in Appendix E.2. The parallel scan, hard-reset dynamics, spike-time solvers, and readout remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use latency-encoded MNIST, SHD, SSC, and Yin-Yang, including the same sub-millisecond temporal-coding scenario. Higher input-spike consumption reflects the revised method within existing coverage, not a new dataset or task.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the same Göltz, Wunderlich–Pehle, Hammouamri, and Mészáros comparisons in their respective datasets. The sequential event-based runtime baseline and the Hammouamri/Mészáros comparisons in Appendix Table 5 are also unchanged.

E3.justification: Table 2 specifies the added regularization weight as 5e-05 for SHD/SSC and zero for MNIST/Yin-Yang, changing the SHD/SSC training configuration. Other reported budgets, metrics, preprocessing protocols, and timing procedures are retained. Replacing SHD's hidden-size entry with 'varies' reflects sizes already evaluated in v1.

E4.justification: Appendix G revises the existing five-run diagnostics of input consumption, output activity, and retained work in Figures 11–13 alongside the new regularizer. These revisit the existing efficiency questions; no separate controlled ablation isolates the added penalty. The chunk-size, solver-convergence, and temporal-discretization analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report accuracy means and standard deviations over five seeds, timing averages over 100 batches and three runs, and five-run work diagnostics. Changed accuracy standard deviations are revised estimates, not a change in uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Table 1 changes SHD-256 accuracy from 94.78 (0.56) to 94.77 (0.46), SHD-512 from 95.10 (0.20) to 94.96 (0.23), and SSC-512 from 77.35 (0.23) to 77.79 (0.19). These accompany a changed training objective. Figures 11–13 report approximately 100% input consumption, versus earlier first-layer averages of 94–96% and SHD second-layer averages around 98%, with revised activity/work trajectories. MNIST accuracy and Appendix F timing/memory results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix E.1 introduces mathematical definitions for the individual over-firing penalty in Equations 53–54 and extends Equation 46. The existing ODE solutions, associativity proof, readout derivations, and implicit-gradient derivation are retained. Moving the affine-composition derivation into Section 3.2.1 does not add new theory.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: parallel processing with exact hard resets, up to 44x acceleration, differentiable continuous-time spike solvers, and demonstrations on four datasets. Revised supporting results do not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: Appendices E.1–E.2 now attribute near-complete queue consumption to penalizing individual overactive neurons, replacing v1's proposed future remedy. Section 3.2.2 also adds the broader statement that there is only one spike time between input spikes; this needs qualification because the retained Appendix E.2 explicitly allows repeated post-reset spikes before the next input.

D1.justification: The Software and Data section replaces a promised future code release with reported availability and a repository link. Table 2 supplies the new regularizer's weights. Appendix E.4 explicitly documents ignoring zero-valued MNIST pixels, and E.2 adds ceiling notation to the later-layer chunk budget; these documentation refinements do not independently establish implementation changes.

R1.justification: The cited works and bibliography are unchanged. The positioning relative to reset-modifying parallel methods, discrete-time approaches, and analytical spike-time solutions retains the same substance.

P1.justification: Section 3.2 gains descriptive paragraph headings and a clearer solver roadmap. Affine-composition equations and spike-detection checks move from the appendices into the main explanation. Additional copyediting, terminology adjustments, and publication/acknowledgment updates are limited; the overall section structure remains.

P2.justification: Figure 4 corrects the chunk brackets to show overlap at the reprocessed fourth spike. Figures 11–13 have revised curves, axis ranges, and captions, while Table 2 gains a regularizer row. Existing figures and tables shift with reflow, but the overall display organization is retained.

improvement.justification: The added regularizer addresses v1's acknowledged incomplete input consumption, with Figures 11–13 reporting near-complete consumption at unchanged spike caps. Clearer method organization, the corrected Figure 4, and concrete code-access information improve usability and reproducibility. Accuracy revisions are small and mixed, and the new single-spike-per-interval wording introduces a limited inconsistency with Appendix E.2. The practical and documentation gains nevertheless support a modest net improvement.
